# Second Brainstorm — Evidence-Driven Expansion

The Awtsmoos narrows infinite possibility into measurable light;
Awtsmoos.com chooses improvements that make crawler truth and human structure unite.

## Generation-3 implementation families

### Family 1: semantic runtime completion
- Verify JSON-LD/social-title behavior through fresh server 8939.
- Add idempotence runtime check.
- Add schema-type tests for app/game/public-information pages.

### Family 2: coverage auditor
- Build a small read-only audit module from current generated metadata + sitemap artifacts.
- Report registered metadata records, sitemap coverage, redirect-prone paths, duplicate canonicals, missing semantic headings.
- Produce JSON and text output for CI/developer use.
- No network calls inside the static auditor; runtime crawl remains a separate acceptance script.

### Family 3: runtime crawl acceptance
- Walk root sitemap indexes with bounded concurrency.
- Follow only same-origin public URLs.
- Check HTTP status, redirects, canonical, robots, title, H1 presence, JSON-LD presence where expected.
- Keep this as a test/diagnostic tool, not production request work.

### Family 4: comment fixture depth
- Add >500 aliases fixture to prove pagination.
- Add >10,000 pointers fixture to prove shard splitting.
- Verify roots and replies share canonical comment route.

### Family 5: alias structured identity
- Evaluate `ProfilePage` JSON-LD from validated public alias data.
- Only include public display name, canonical URL, description, optional public website.
- Never expose private activity ledger or internal IDs beyond the already-public alias ID.

### Family 6: post structured identity
- Evaluate breadcrumb and article JSON-LD using fields already fetched for SSR.
- Avoid extra database calls.
- Preserve existing canonical/noindex logic.

### Family 7: translation integrity
- Add deterministic corpus validator for manifest→bundle coordinates and row uniqueness.
- Record missing title source as explicit limitation.

### Family 8: developer architecture docs
- Explain public-content families, static/dynamic split, exclusions, performance constraints, test commands, deployment proof.
